title: Non-evolutionary effects on period change in Magellanic Cepheids. III. Empirical connection with additional low-amplitude variability
comment: Accepted for publication in A&A. 15 pages (including 4 appendices), 10 figures, 5 tables
summary: The O-C method in classical Cepheids traces both evolutionary and shorter-timescale (non-evolutionary) period changes. In our previous works, we found irregular period changes in $\sim$33% of Magellanic classical Cepheids, but excluded Cepheids showing additional low-amplitude variability. Here, we establish whether first-overtone Cepheids hosting such variability differ in their period-change behaviour from the general first-overtone population. We analyse 544 Magellanic Cepheids with period ratios $P_{\rm x}/P_{\rm 1O} \sim 0.60-0.65$ or $P_{\rm 1O}/P_{\rm x} \sim 0.68$, using OGLE photometry, and classify and characterise their O-C diagrams following our previous studies. We find irregular period changes in 339 first-overtone Cepheids (195 in the LMC and 144 in the SMC), an incidence rate of $\sim$75.5%, a statistically significant increase over the $\sim$68.1% of our previous single-mode first-overtone sample. The combined first-overtone incidence becomes $\sim$69.7%. This provides the first empirical connection between additional low-amplitude variability and irregular period changes in first-overtone Cepheids. At a fixed pulsation period, the irregularity strength anticorrelates with the dominant pulsation amplitude but not with the additional-signal amplitude, suggesting that the additional periodicity marks a weakly saturated pulsation state rather than driving the irregularity. We further detect cycle-to-cycle (C2C) period variation in 37% of the class 3 sample, with jitter roughly seven times larger than in non-Blazhko RRc stars and a shallower scaling with pulsation period.

title: Euclid: Data Release 1 (DR1) -- Bayesian 3D shape inference of star-forming galaxy populations
comment: Paper intended for the A&A Special Issue "Euclid First Data Release'', Submitted to A&A, 31 pages, 33 figures
summary: Understanding the intrinsic 3D shapes of galaxies provides crucial insights into their formation and evolution, but determining these from projections remains challenging. We apply a Bayesian inference framework to optical images of galaxies from the Euclid Data Release 1, leveraging its large sample size to test the scalability and robustness of this methodology. Applying Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) sampling to Sérsic axis ratios and effective radii, we constrain the population-level mean 3D ellipticity, triaxiality, and size, together with their covariances for $40\,864\,304$ star-forming galaxies with stellar masses $M_\ast=10^{9}$--$10^{10.5}M_\odot$ at redshifts $0<z<1.2$. Our sample size exceeds previous shape inference studies by factors of $440$--$52\,800$ relative to early observations by JWST, and factors of $440$--$17\,600$ relative to legacy observations from HST in overlapping mass-redshift bins, enabling finer binning alongside improved statistical constraints on shape evolution. We additionally include over 9 million galaxies at $z<0.5$, a regime historically limited by sample size in previous shape inference studies. We recover key evolutionary trends identified in previous smaller-sample studies. We find high ellipticities ($μ_E \sim 0.600$--$0.821$) across all bins, indicating that the underlying 3D shape distributions are statistically dominated by flattened geometries. Most notably, we recover the decline of the prolate fraction towards $z=0$ at low masses ($M_\ast=10^{9}$--$10^{9.5}M_\odot$) reported by previous studies. This trend is seen consistently in comparable analyses of independent data sets spanning different depths and resolution regimes, showing that it is not an artefact of small-sample statistics, suggesting it may be a genuine feature of galaxy evolution. We also identify future methodological improvements for subsequent Euclid data releases.

title: OGLE Pre-discovery Observations of the Dwarf Planet Candidate 2026 ED138
comment: submitted to Acta Astronomica
summary: The newly discovered trans-Neptunian object, 2026 ED138, is a strong dwarf planet candidate detected by the Vera C. Rubin Observatory. Despite its high intrinsic brightness, it evaded detection by previous sky surveys as it hid near crowded Galactic disk fields. Here, we present an analysis of precovery observations of 2026 ED138 in archival data from the Optical Gravitational Lensing Experiment (OGLE). We identify 102 reliable detections of the object as it moved across the dense regions of the Galactic plane and bulge between 2011 and 2024. We provide precise astrometric and photometric measurements of the object. Modeling its phase curve yields absolute magnitudes of H_I = 2.224 +/- 0.034 mag and H_V = 3.154 +/- 0.035 mag. Period analysis of the phase-angle-corrected light curve reveals a candidate rotation period of 1.18077 days and its 1-day alias 0.54066 days, although a low signal-to-noise ratio renders these periodicities tentative.

title: Starspots on eclipsing giant stars II.: TESS continuous viewing zone giant V521 Dra
comment: Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics (18 pages, 17 figures)
summary: Eclipsing binaries are exceptional laboratories for stellar astrophysics. By analysing the modulations in their eclipse light curves, we can probe their surface inhomogeneities. The eclipse-mapping technique enables us to scan starspots in detail, using the transit of a companion star across the surface of a spotted star. When multiple consecutive eclipses are observed, this method may also reveal the evolution of spot properties and provide evidence for stellar differential rotation. We study the magnetic activity of V521 Dra, a tidally locked eclipsing binary with a red giant primary and a main-sequence secondary, both of K spectral class, on a 4.27 d orbit. This is an exceptional system with ~5.3 years of TESS 2 min cadence observations. This offers a unique opportunity to study magnetic activity in uninterrupted blocks over several years with very high photometric precision. We aim to constrain the evolution of the spot pattern of V521 Dra A. We used two methods to study the spot activity of the primary: eclipse mapping and analytic spot modelling. We analysed the stellar properties of the system with a set of methods, including combined modelling of the eclipse light curves, radial velocity data, spectral energy distribution analysis, and forward modelling of the whole orbital light curve. The star shows strong spot-induced modulations both in the eclipse and out-of-eclipse parts of the light curve. We identified 540 spot eclipse signals in 203 primary eclipses. Eclipse mapping reveals the presence of up to four spots. The spot longitudes drift continuously in time, indicating differential rotation. Spots in the eclipse-mapping data show differing angular velocities in their drift, implying a near-surface shear in the convective zone of the primary. Using time series spectroscopy and the spectral energy distribution, we constrained the astrophysical parameters of the binary system.

title: MeerKAT and ASKAP EMU new radio-continuum observations of Wolf-Rayet nebula PCG 11 (Cohen's Ring)
comment: accepted for publication in the Serbian Astronomical Journal
summary: We present new radio-continuum observations of the well-known Wolf-Rayet (WR) nebula PCG 11 (Cohen's Ring; named after and in honour of the co-author on the discovery paper, Martin Cohen) using observations from the Australian Square Kilometre Array Pathfinder (ASKAP) Evolutionary Map of the Universe (EMU), Australia Telescope Compact Array (ATCA) and MeerKAT surveys. We find that the elliptical shell surrounding Cohen's Ring has a flux density of 62$\pm$2\,mJy at 1000 MHz. The angular size of the elliptical emission is measured to be 54\arcsec$\times$45\arcsec\ (at P.A.=69.4\D), which agrees well with observations of the source in H$α$ and at 24\,$μ$m in the infrared. Using the measured angular size and a distance of 3.94$\pm$0.27\,kpc, we determine that the nebula has a linear size of $1.03(\pm0.07)\times0.86(\pm0.06)$\,pc. Together with our new and previously measured flux density estimates, we determine a spectral index for Cohen's Ring to be $α$=0.06$\pm$0.02, indicating that the emission from the WR nebula is of thermal origin. Based on a typical average expansion velocity of 75~km~s$^{-1}$ for a WR star with a Red Supergiant (RSG) progenitor, we estimate the age of Cohen's Ring to be $\sim$ 13500 years. Our NANTEN telescope CO observations suggest that Cohen's Ring was formed during a relatively recent mass-loss event, while the associated CO-emitting molecular gas reflects the cumulative effects of stellar-wind feedback over a much longer timescale ($\sim$1.5\,Myr). As one of the few WR ring nebulae with linked molecular gas, Cohen's Ring provides a valuable laboratory for studying the long-term impact of massive-star feedback on surrounding molecular clouds.

title: Crater Scaling Relationships for Gas Impingement on Planetary Regolith
comment: 45 pages, 12 figures, submitted to the Planetary Science Journal
summary: Plume-surface interaction (PSI) effects remains a major uncertainty for operations on regolith-covered planetary bodies. Although spacecraft exhaust can erode surfaces, form craters, and accelerate ejecta, existing PSI relationships are largely derived for scenario-specific lunar and Martian landing conditions and are not yet reliably generalizable. Resolving this problem is important not only for spacecraft safety, but also because controlled thruster interactions could provide an active geotechnical experiment during asteroid reconnaissance. Measurements of thruster-formed craters and ejecta may constrain regolith density, strength, porosity, and particle properties that are otherwise difficult to determine remotely. Such information is particularly relevant to planetary defense, where uncertainty in near-surface properties can strongly affect the outcome of kinetic-impact mitigation and the interpretation of momentum transfer. We investigate gas-driven excavation using near-vacuum, pulsed-N$_2$ experiments in a cohesionless asteroid regolith analog and comparisons with a low-gravity drop-tower experiment and historical chemical-thruster tests. We adapt projectile-cratering $π$-scaling, and find that these relationships can describe gas crater volume as a function of gas, target, gravity, and nozzle properties. A common gravity-regime relationship describes the laboratory data and is consistent with an experimental low-gravity result. Generalizing the $π$-scaling relationship for cohesive targets shows consistency with Apollo-era chemical-thruster cases. These results provide a framework for using spacecraft thrusters as active geotechnical tools during small-body reconnaissance.

title: AGB Atmospheres in Binary Environments: A First Step with CO5BOLB
comment: 18 pages, submitted to Astronomy and Astrophysics
summary: Asymptotic Giant Branch (AGB) stars are characterized by complex atmospheric dynamics driven by convection and pulsations. In binary systems, the presence of a companion can further influence these dynamics, potentially affecting mass-loss processes and the morphology of the circumstellar environment, yet this influence on the atmosphere itself remains poorly quantified. This study aims to fill this gap by employing CO5BOLD simulations with a modified gravitational potential to explore how companion mass affects the atmospheric structure of AGB stars. We used radiative hydrodynamics (RHD) simulations with CO5BOLD to model the convective interior and atmosphere of AGB stars. We modified the gravitational potential to include a secondary mass and a centrifugal term, representing the companion as a point-mass potential on a steady, tidally locked circular orbit outside the computational domain, with the Coriolis force neglected. We performed simulations with different companion masses and using singular value decomposition (SVD), we identified the spatial distribution of pulsation energy and quantified its properties. We also examined the density structure to identify anisotropies induced by the companion. We isolate two dynamically distinct regimes, a pulsation-dominated layer and an outer, low-frequency outflow region, whose pulsation properties remain largely unaffected by the companion: their frequency, amplitude, and coherence stay consistent across all models. The density structure, by contrast, responds clearly to the companion, forming a pronounced anisotropy along the binary axis that strengthens with companion mass. This indicates that the intrinsic pulsational dynamics of the AGB star dominate over the tidal influence of the companion within the explored parameter space, while the density structure remains the most sensitive tracer of binarity.

title: Globular Clusters in the Time of JWST. II. Looks like the second, moves like the first: the syrphid-like intermediate population of NGC 2808
comment: 16 pages, 12 figures, submitted to MNRAS, comments welcome
summary: The present-day kinematics of multiple populations in globular clusters can retain information about their initial conditions and can therefore help trace how the different populations formed. We combine JWST and HST photometry and proper motions to study the internal dynamics of four populations in NGC 2808 out to about eight half-light radii: the first population (1P) and three second-population groups with increasing light-element processing (2Pa, 2Pb, and 2Pc), providing the first detailed kinematic characterisation of the chemically intermediate 2Pa. We find significant kinematic differences between the populations. While all four have similar sky-projected radial velocity dispersions, 2Pb and 2Pc have lower tangential dispersions than 1P and are strongly radially anisotropic, whereas 2Pa shares the only mildly anisotropic kinematics of 1P. Therefore, chemically distinct 2P groups have different dynamical properties, suggesting that they formed under different conditions and/or experienced a different subsequent dynamical evolution. In the outer JWST field, the velocity dispersion depends only weakly on stellar mass, with hints of inverted equipartition. The difference between radial and tangential equipartition is similar for 1P and 2Pa and decreases towards 2Pc, a trend that remains tentative given the uncertainties. Our results show that 2P is not a dynamically homogeneous group, and that the kinematics of its individual groups provide a key constraint for multiple population formation scenarios.

title: A Bright L4 Neptune Trojan Found by Stacking Archival ZTF Images
summary: We report a Neptune Trojan found by a shift-and-stack search of archival Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF) difference images of 2019 October, and recovered in public images of seven other telescopes back to 2008. The orbit uses 88 positions on 54 nights from 2008 to 2025, a 17.22-year arc, all measured on our own Gaia DR3 plate solutions. Its heliocentric osculating elements at JD 2460000.5 are a = 30.2158 +/- 0.0004 au, e = 0.0661 and i = 20.32 deg; a fit of the same positions with the independent orbit code Find_Orb agrees within 0.4 sigma in every element. The nominal orbit librates about Neptune's leading Lagrange point L4 with a period of 9.25 kyr and an amplitude of 8.7 deg over the next Myr, and 84 +/- 2% of 500 clones of the orbit remain L4 Trojans for 4.5 Gyr. Its absolute magnitude is H_V = 6.96 +/- 0.10 (linear phase law), or 6.81 +/- 0.06 on the H, G convention of the Minor Planet Center's list of Neptune Trojans, whose brightest L4 member has H = 7.26, so the object is possibly the brightest known L4 Neptune Trojan. Its color, g-r = 0.52 +/- 0.05, lies in the g-r range of the red Neptune Trojans, and for albedos of 0.05-0.15 its diameter is about 140-240 km.

title: Observational constraints on CO sequestration and disk mass in the planet-hosting PDS 70 disk
comment: Accepted for publication in A&A
summary: Exoplanets accrete gas, dust, and ice from their natal environment, setting the chemical composition of their atmospheres and interiors. The abundance of the major volatiles in disks can be used to possibly link exoplanet atmospheres to their formation location in the disk. In this work, we aim to quantify the peak CO abundance and disk mass of the PDS 70 disk, the first disk with a direct confirmation of two accreting planets in its dust cavity. We present the first detection of N$_2$H$^+$ and C$^{17}$O in this disk. The C$^{17}$O emission shows marginal statistical evidence for an azimuthal asymmetry trailing that previously seen in the continuum emission. We then compare the disk integrated fluxes of N$_2$H$^+$, CO isotopologues, and the continuum to an existing grid of thermochemical models. We find that the derived disk mass drops by a factor of $\sim 3.4$ from $0.039^{+0.067}_{-0.018}$ M$_{\odot}$ to $0.011^{+0.011}_{-0.006}$ M$_{\odot}$ if the C$^{17}$O line flux is included in the fitting procedure; the quoted intervals do not include systematic uncertainties. CO on the other hand is sequestered with an effective abundance of $(4.8^{+4.3}_{-2.7} - 17^{+8}_{-8}) \times 10^{-6}$ relative to H$_2$ in the probed disk layers after accounting for CO freeze-out and isotope selective CO photodissociation for the adopted chemical network and ionization prescription. The range in peak CO abundances reflects the uncertainty in the N$_2$H$^+$ emission, assuming either optically thin emission at 21 K or optically thick emission. Therefore, the PDS 70 planets are possibly accreting the final portion of their atmospheres from the outer disk molecular layer where CO is sequestered. Thus, CO sequestering may need to be considered when interpreting the chemical composition of planetary atmospheres.

title: Machine-Learning Reconstruction of Intergalactic Medium Column-Density Maps from Observed Ly$α$ Emission Cubes
comment: 35 pages, 20 figures. Accepted for publication in The Astrophysical Journal (ApJ)
summary: Understanding the large-scale structure of the intergalactic medium (IGM) is essential for studying galaxy evolution, particularly at $z \sim 2$--$6$, when cold filaments in the cosmic web are considered a primary mechanism for fueling galaxy growth. At these redshifts, Ly$α$ emission shifts into the optical regime and serves as the primary tracer of diffuse IGM for ground-based integral field units (IFUs). However, detections remain limited by low signal-to-noise ratios (S/N) and the complexities of resonant scattering. We present a proof-of-concept machine-learning framework to reconstruct IGM gas column-density maps from noisy Ly$α$ IFU emission cubes. Using Keck Cosmic Web Imager (KCWI) observations of $z \sim 2.3$ protoclusters as a case study, we train a custom convolutional neural network (CNN), the Column Density Estimator (CDE), on a simulated dataset combining IllustrisTNG100 with simplified radiative-transfer calculations and an approximate treatment of KCWI noise. The CDE successfully reconstructs broad filamentary structures in the simulated test set under these adopted assumptions. Applied to observed KCWI data, the CDE predicts gas column-density maps containing filamentary structures extending over $\gtrsim 40''$ ($\sim 1$ comoving Mpc), consistent with an IGM interpretation. The observed reconstructions remain conditional on the adopted models. These results illustrate the potential of the CDE framework for connecting diffuse Ly$α$ observations with simulations of the IGM.

title: The ZTF Variability Archive (ZVAR): Initial Data Release (DR1)
comment: 14 pages, 6 figures, submitted to PASP, data is available at https://zvar.caltech.edu
summary: The Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF) has observed the northern sky observable from Palomar Observatory since March 2018, accumulating a median of a thousand photometric measurements across $gri$ for each of more than a billion sources. Among these billions of objects are millions of periodically variable stars, active galactic nuclei, stellar remnants, and substellar objects. We describe the initial data release (DR1) of the ZTF Variability Archive (ZVAR) which provides image difference forced photometry, candidate periods, and variability metrics for approximately 1.3 billion sources in ZTF having an identification in Pan-STARRS1 DR1 (PS1). The data cover the 5.37 year interval between March 2018 and July 2023. ZVAR is sensitive to periods between 5 minutes and 2.7 years. We also describe tools for accessing the ZVAR data.

title: Dwarfs of Fire and Ice: UV-Irradiation-Driven Thermal Inversion, Disequilibrium Chemistry, and a Cloud-Free Atmosphere in a Strongly Irradiated Brown Dwarf Probed by JWST/NIRSpec Phase-Resolved Spectroscopy
comment: Accepted for publication in ApJ on November 5, 2026. 25 pages, 16 figures
summary: We present time-resolved JWST/NIRSpec PRISM spectrophotometry of the white dwarf (WD)-brown dwarf (BD) binary SDSS J141126.20+200911.1 (SDSS1411). Close WD-BD binaries provide powerful laboratories for studying the effects of stellar irradiation on substellar atmospheres because of their high companion-to-host flux ratios, short orbital periods, and intense UV irradiation from the WD. We measure strong wavelength-dependent variability, with day-night relative flux variations reaching ~280%. The SDSS1411B phase curves are well described by a second-order Fourier model, and correlations among the Fourier amplitudes suggest larger flux and temperature variations in the upper atmosphere. Non-irradiated forward models under chemical equilibrium do not reproduce the observed phase-resolved SDSS1411B spectra, indicating substantial departures from isolated-BD atmospheric structures. In contrast, atmospheric retrievals successfully reproduce both the dayside and nightside spectra. The retrievals reveal a prominent dayside temperature inversion, favor cloud-free atmospheres, and provide evidence for CO2 disequilibrium chemistry. An energy-budget analysis indicates low day-to-night heat redistribution efficiency and constrains the BD cooling age to ~3 Gyr, while the inferred BD radius is significantly more compact than predicted by BD evolutionary models. These results reveal the rich atmospheric dynamics and disequilibrium chemistry of a UV-irradiated BD and demonstrate the power of full-orbit JWST phase-resolved spectroscopy for constraining the atmospheric physics of strongly irradiated substellar objects.

title: B-fields And Dust in InterstelLar FiLAments Using Dust POLarization (BALLAD-POL): V. Magnetic Fields and Grain Alignment Mechanisms in Serpens Main Using JCMT/POL-2 Polarization
comment: Accepted for publication in ApJ. 22 Pages, 17 Figures
summary: We investigate magnetic fields ($B$-field) and grain alignment mechanisms in Serpens Main using 850 $μ$m dust polarization observations from JCMT/POL-2. We derive a map of $B$-field strength and calculate the mass-to-flux ratio and Alfvénic Mach number, suggesting the subdominance of $B$-fields over gravity but their dominance over turbulence. Fitting the Ricean mean model to the nondebiased polarization fraction ($P$) as a function of emission intensity ($I$) yields a slope $α= 0.68\pm0.01$, revealing depolarization. To understand its origins, we examine the dependence of $P$ on gas column density ($N({\rm H}_{2})$), dust temperature ($T_{\rm d}$), and polarization angle dispersion function ($S$). We find no correlation between $P$ and $S$, whereas for $P\times S$, an observational proxy for alignment efficiency decreases with increasing $N({\rm H}_{2})$. This suggests that $B$-field tangling is not the primary cause of depolarization and instead points to reduced grain alignment in denser regions. To test this interpretation within radiative torque (RAT) alignment theory, we calculate the minimum size of aligned grains ($a_{\rm align}$) and magnetic relaxation strength ($δ_{\rm mag,sp}$) using $N({\rm H}_{2})$, $T_{\rm d}$, and our estimated $B$-field map. We find that both $P$ and $P \times S$ decrease with increasing $a_{\rm align}$, supporting reduced grain alignment as the main cause of depolarization in Serpens Main. However, neither $P$ nor $P \times S$ shows a correlation with $δ_{\rm mag,sp}$, suggesting that enhanced grain alignment due to magnetic relaxation is insufficient to compensate for the reduced alignment associated with increasing $a_{\rm align}$ toward denser regions.

title: C$_2$ Swan, CH and CN emission, surface temperature and luminous efficiency of the Hayabusa2 sample-return capsule from ground-based spectroscopy
comment: 42 pages, 15 figures, 3 tables. Submitted to Earth, Planets and Space. Data and movies: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24125212
summary: The Hayabusa2 sample-return capsule entered the atmosphere over South Australia on 5 December 2020 at 12 km/s. A slitless spectral video, taken from the ground with a hand-tracked consumer camera, shows the capsule alone from 80 to 49 km. In the first ten seconds of heating the shock layer emits the CN violet system, the CH A-X band and the C$_2$ Swan bands, the latter for the first time in remote observations of a capsule entry. C$_2$ ($T_{\rm rot}\approx9200$ K, $T_{\rm vib}\approx7800$ K) and CN (about 7000 K) are far hotter than the surface. C$_2$ and CH disappear while the heat flux is still rising and CN persists, which we relate to the early pyrolysis of the carbon-phenolic ablator and to the changing boundary-layer chemistry. The colour temperature of the heat shield rises from 2720 to 3080 K, in agreement with airborne results. The radiated energy is one to two orders of magnitude below that of natural fireballs, because the light comes from the hot surface rather than from ablation vapour. A faint persistent train lights up about 1 s after the passage and fades within a few seconds, probably chemiluminescence in the cooling wake.

title: The Closest Super-Eccentric Giant Planet: Dynamical History and Orbital Future of Gaia-3b
comment: 15 pages, 5 figures. Accepted for publication in AJ
summary: With new high-resolution spectra and radial velocities (RVs) from the NEID spectrometer, we reaffirm the planetary designation of the previously identified super-eccentric giant planet Gaia~3b. Our additional 23 RVs span 356 days, including an RV observation obtained within hours of the periastron passage. By modeling all of the available RVs we collapse a previously tri-modal orbital period posterior distribution and report a more precisely measured value of $P=331.52\pm0.02$ days. Our measure of the eccentricity ($e=0.9462\pm0.0017$) is in agreement with previous measurements and thus corroborates the status of Gaia~3b as the third most eccentric planet known to date. We generate synthetic realizations of the Gaia astrometric time series and derived RUWE to show that only the planetary-companion and close to equal-mass binary cases are plausible when compared to the reported RUWE. We then show that the close to equal-mass binary case is unlikely based on the Gaia color-magnitude position and the shape and amplitude of the bisectors measured from the NEID cross-correlation functions. The confirmation of Gaia~3b's planetary status makes it the closest known super-eccentric giant planet ($d \approx 35$ pc) and leads us to anticipate that Gaia DR4 will detect more super-eccentric planets orbiting nearby Sun-like stars. Finally, due to the presence of a distant stellar companion, we demonstrate that a plausible pathway exists for excitation of the planet's eccentricity by von Zeipel-Kozai-Lidov oscillations.

title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). The PHZ processing function for the physical properties of galaxies
comment: 13 pages, 8 figures. Paper intended for the A\&A Special Issue "Euclid First Data Release''
summary: Euclid is a European Space Agency mission mapping the extragalactic sky, aiming to provide the most-accurate 3D view of the Universe at optical and near-infrared wavelengths, by measuring the photometric redshifts of billions of galaxies. Within the Euclid Consortium, this task is executed by the PHZ Organisation Unit. PHZ takes as input the multi-wavelength photometry of Euclid and ground-based data, and returns as output the source classification, photometric redshifts for the Euclid core science (i.e., cosmology), and photometric redshifts plus physical parameters and absolute magnitudes for non-cosmological science. As part of the first Euclid Data Release (DR1), we describe the details of the DR1 pipeline for non-cosmological science, along with the released data products, and their validation. The non-cosmological science data products are obtained with NNPZ, a nearest-neighbour algorithm developed within PHZ that infers the properties of each target galaxy from its closest matches, in colour-magnitude space, within a reference sample of galaxies with known redshifts and physical parameters. We built this reference sample from Euclid observations of COSMOS, one of the Euclid Auxiliary Fields, labelling each galaxy with redshifts and physical parameters derived from the COSMOS2020 multi-wavelength photometry, consistently with the Euclid core-science results. Combined with the adjustments and priors required to generalise the results across the entire extragalactic sky, this approach yields high-quality and internally consistent data products. We tested the performance using both internal metrics and comparisons to ancillary data sets (e.g., COSMOS2020, 3D-HST, and DESI) and scaling relations (e.g., the star-forming main sequence); the results are in line with expectations and pre-DR1 simulations for both the Euclid Wide Survey and Euclid Deep Fields.

title: Mitigating variance shrinkage in multi-task galaxy property inference from imaging data via statistical manifold alignment
comment: 12 pages, 5 figures, 2 tables, accepted by A&A
summary: Inferring photometric redshifts ($z$) and key stellar population properties ($\log(M_*/\mathrm{M}_\odot)$, $D_n4000$, and $\mathrm{H}δ_A$) directly from multi-band imaging is increasingly critical for spectroscopically limited large surveys such as LSST and CSST. However, conventional point-wise loss functions (e.g., mean squared error or Huber loss) employed in deep neural networks often induce ``variance shrinkage''---a regression-to-the-mean effect that contracts predicted variances, distorts non-linear physical manifolds (such as bimodal distributions), and truncates heavy-tail populations. Here, we present ViTMultiTask, a vision transformer framework that incorporates a multi-scale maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) loss to enforce higher-order joint distribution alignment in reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS). Trained on 83,846 galaxies from Subaru HSC five-band ($g,r,i,z,y$) imaging cross-matched with DESI Data Release 1 Bright Galaxy Survey spectra, the model achieves high point-estimate precision on an independent test set of 5,000 galaxies: $σ_{\mathrm{NMAD}} = 0.020$ for $z$, $0.169\,\mathrm{dex}$ for $\log(M_*/\mathrm{M}_\odot)$, $0.073$ for $D_n4000$, and $1.185\,\text{Å}$ for $\mathrm{H}δ_A$. Ablation experiments demonstrate that incorporating the MMD loss effectively mitigates variance shrinkage and more accurately reproduces the observed spectroscopic parameter distributions (including bimodal structures and heavy tails), while maintaining point-estimate accuracy statistically consistent with the baseline (RMSE changes $\le 3.5\%$) and catastrophic outlier rates fully comparable to the baseline. This kernel-based manifold alignment offers a statistically grounded and practical paradigm for comprehensive galaxy property inference in the deep imaging era.

title: La Silla-QUEST RR Lyrae Survey III: The Shape of the Outer Virgo Overdensity
comment: 24 pages, 13 figures, 1 machine readable table, submitted to Astrophysical Journal
summary: Using the La Silla-QUEST and Gaia surveys, we identify 256 RR Lyrae stars (RRLS) in the Outer Virgo Overdensity (OVOD). These show that the OVOD has a signifcantly larger and more complex shape than previously recognized. The OVOD lies at an average distance of $\sim 85$ kpc, has a long dimension of $\sim 57^\circ$ ($\sim 85$ kpc), and a width that varies from $\sim 10^\circ $ ($\sim 15$ kpc) to $\sim 35^\circ $ ($\sim 50$ kpc) in a prominent bulge. Because it bends by $\sim 35^\circ$ from a great circle, it does not appear to be a stellar stream. The type ab RRLS (RRab) span a large range in period, with a mean of $0.59$ days, and only $19\pm 3 \%$ lie near the locus of Oosterhoff II variables in the Bailey diagram. The overall large number of RRLS along with a mean RRab metallicity ([Fe/H]) of -1.60 and $1 σ$ dispersion of 0.32, as inferred from the RRab periods, suggest that the OVOD progenitor was a large dwarf galaxy. The hypothesis that the OVOD may be a shell produced by the Gaia-Sausage-Enceladus merger \citep{chandra2023} is supported by the $\sim 70^\circ$ angle that the southern extension of the OVOD makes with the orbits of red giants in its central part. The complex shape of the overall RRLS distribution, including a small north-south distance gradient, may also indicate, however, that we are seeing a blended, composite structure projected on the sky.

title: The Black Hole Mass of the Sunflower Galaxy NGC 5055: Direct Measurement via Stellar Kinematics with Keck/OSIRIS Laser Guide Star Adaptive Optics
comment: 20 pages, 11 figures, 4 tables; accepted for publication in The Astrophysical Journal
summary: We present the first stellar-dynamical supermassive black hole mass measurement in the nearby spiral galaxy NGC 5055 (M63) using near-infrared integral-field spectroscopy with Keck/OSIRIS assisted by the laser guide star adaptive optics system. The observations deliver two-dimensional stellar kinematics extracted from the CO bandhead absorption features via pPXF at an angular resolution of $0.045''$. The stellar velocity dispersion rises steeply from $\sim90~{\rm km~s^{-1}}$ at $r\sim1''$ to a central peak of $\sim135~{\rm km~s^{-1}}$, kinematically tracing the gravitational influence of a central mass concentration. Modeling these kinematics with an ensemble of four JAM models, spanning cylindrical and spherical velocity-ellipsoid alignments and two independent MGE decompositions of archival HST imaging, yields a black hole mass of $M_{\rm BH}=4.56^{+1.73}_{-1.82}\times10^6~{\rm M_\odot}$. The stellar orbits are consistent with near-isotropy ($β\approx0$), typical of rotating late-type galaxies. NGC 5055 emerges as a remarkable local analogue to the Milky Way in terms of its black hole, nuclear star cluster, and total stellar mass. The surface brightness profile of NGC 5055 shows no evidence for a classical bulge; if confirmed bulgeless, NGC 5055 would join the rare class of spirals with a direct dynamical $M_{\rm BH}$ determination in the absence of a bulge, a regime currently populated by only a handful of galaxies including NGC 2748 and NGC 4395. This measurement provides a new anchor for black hole scaling relations in late-type galaxies at the low-mass end of the black hole mass spectrum.

title: Active Learning for Molecular Discovery: A Retrospective Test toward TMC-1
comment: 13 pages, 3 figures, 3 tables; submitted to ApJ; code and data at doi:10.5281/zenodo.23312984
summary: Machine-learning recommendation lists can help prioritize searches for new interstellar molecules, but whether reranking such a list as detections accumulate improves on it has not been tested. We present a pre-registered retrospective test toward TMC-1, using a published machine-learning list of 1,510 recommended candidates, consolidated to 1,434 candidates, and the species reported there through September 2026. At four annual origins from 2022 to 2025, a logistic-regression ranking on seven released features, refit on the detections known at each origin, separates later detections from never-detected candidates with a pooled AUC of 0.867, against 0.706 for the best single-criterion baseline (difference 0.160; 95\% interval 0.095-0.230). The advantage persists under a shifted date boundary and two alternative feature regimes, but is not established among the top 100 candidates (12 versus 7 detections). A searcher that refits on its own observations reaches half of the 63 detected species on the list in a median of 200 observations, against 332 for the best fixed ordering and 717.5 expected for random search. Uncertainty sampling, the standard active-learning rule, performs worse than random (AUC 0.210): later detections lie at low predictive uncertainty, close to known chemistry. Of 101 species in our validation set, 37 are absent from the list, and only 13 of these appear in a pool rebuilt from its source databases, including 2 of 11 radicals and neither ion. Candidate generation, not ranking, is the main constraint. We release 100 recommended targets, with code and frozen inputs, for prospective testing.

title: The Distant Milky Way Halo from the Southern Hemisphere: Spatially broad and closer stellar debris associated to the Magellanic Stream
comment: 22 pages, 12 figures, submitted to ApJ
summary: The Magellanic Stream (MS) is a gaseous structure extending over $150^\circ$ across the sky, likely formed through interactions between the Large and Small Magellanic Clouds (LMC and SMC) as they fell into the Milky Way (MW). Its predicted stellar counterpart would provide a collisionless record of these interactions, but few candidate members have been identified. To expand this sample, we constructed a catalog of 87,763 distant K-giant candidates using DELVE DR2 and VHS DR5 photometry and Gaia DR3 astrometry, and analyzed VLT and Magellan spectra of 51 targets along the trailing MS. Combining radial velocities, spectrophotometric distances, and proper motions, we identify five new MS candidates at 58--95 kpc. Their metallicities are consistent with the outskirts of the SMC, while orbit integrations in a time-dependent MW--LMC--SMC potential support a possible Magellanic origin. Combined with previously identified candidates, these stars span a substantially broader range of Magellanic latitude than predicted by existing models, suggesting an extended debris field rather than a narrow stream. The candidates also lie predominantly closer than the simulated debris. More recent, less eccentric SMC orbits may help explain this distance discrepancy, although new simulations are required to test their implications for the stellar debris, along with larger spectroscopic samples.

title: Euclid: Data Release 1 (DR1) - First NISP emission-line maps: Methodology, validation, and applications to galaxy evolution
comment: Paper intended for the A&A Special Issue "Euclid First Data Release''. 18 pages, 15 figures
summary: We demonstrate the capability of the slitless spectroscopic mode of the Euclid Near-Infrared Spectrometer and Photometer (NISP) to produce emission-line maps analogous to narrow-band images with user-defined central wavelengths. We present the first such maps of galaxies at $0.4 < z < 0.9$, constructed from blue-grism exposures obtained during the Euclid performance-verification observations of the Cosmic Evolution Survey (COSMOS) field in November 2023. We demonstrate the use of these maps for identifying star-forming clumps, measuring radial star-formation profiles, detecting projected internal velocity gradients, deblending the H$α$--[N II] complex, and assessing spectroscopic redshift measurements. As a first statistical application, we reconstruct the galaxy mass--metallicity relation for 885 galaxies observed with the blue grism at $0.4 < z < 0.9$ by deblending the H$α$--[N II] complex in the emission-line maps, and measure stacked H$α$ radial profiles for 2634 galaxies over the same redshift range. The mass--metallicity relation is consistent with that obtained from the Euclid 1D spectroscopic measurements, demonstrating overall agreement between the two deblending approaches. The recovered H$α$ radial profiles broadly follow the $Y_{\mathrm{E}}$ stellar continuum but remain modestly more extended after matching the $Y_{\mathrm{E}}$ images to the H$α$ PSF, consistent with previous results in the literature. Across the four $Y_{\mathrm{E}}$ size bins, we measure a mean $R_{50,\mathrm{H}α}/R_{50,Y_{\mathrm{E}}}=1.15$.

title: Combining TTVs, RVs, and astrometry to characterize distant giant companions of transiting hot Jupiters: Application to WASP-4
comment: Accepted for publication in A&A. 15 pages, 10 figures, 3 tables
summary: The origins and architectures of hot Jupiter (HJ) systems remain unclear, with potential explanations for the tight orbits being in-situ formation, disk-migration, or high-eccentricity migration. These mechanisms can leave different imprints on the orbital architecture, but tidal interactions act to erase these imprints for HJs, leading to orbital circularization, realignment, and potentially orbital decay. The latter can be mimicked by the introduction of light travel-time effects (LTTE) caused by an outer giant companion, as for WASP-4$\,$b. We examine the WASP-4 system using newly obtained ESO$\,$3.6/HARPS radial velocity (RV) observations and archival transit-timing data, leveraging the LTTE. Furthermore, we present a novel approach of analyzing HJ systems in sight of $\textit{Gaia}$'s Data Release 4. We propose combining RV, transit-timing, and astrometry data, making use of the LTTE as a proxy for the orbital motion of a possible outer companion. We combine and fit all currently available data and simulate $\textit{Gaia}$ DR4 and DR5 astrometric measurements of WASP-4 and perform an injection and recovery procedure to estimate their impact on the recovered planetary parameters of WASP-4$\,$c. The procedure employs a combined model that describes RVs, transit timing variations (TTVs) via the LTTE, and astrometry simultaneously. Analyzing the existing data, we improve the planetary parameters of WASP-4$\,$c, finding a minimum mass of $9.3\pm1.7\,M_\mathrm{Jup}$ with an orbital period of $10\,600^{+1100}_{-1000}\,$d, or about $29\,$yr. Furthermore, we find that there is no significant orbital decay taking place for WASP-4$\,$b. In simulations of $\textit{Gaia}$ DR5, our three-pronged approach reduces the error bars of WASP-4$\,$c's parameters by about $10\%$, $25\%$, and $33\%$ for its orbital period, time of inferior conjunction, and RV semi-amplitude, respectively. title: VISTA Magellanic Clouds deep observations of Classical Cepheids: Precision distances and a collision-driven SMC
comment: Accepted for publication on A&A. 20 pages, 17 figures
summary: The central regions of the Magellanic Clouds are crucial for understanding galaxy interactions and calibrating the cosmic distance scale, yet they remain observationally challenging due to extreme stellar crowding. We utilised deep VISTA observations (VMCDeep) to determine the highest-precision near-infrared Period-Luminosity (PL) and Period-Wesenheit (PW) relations to date for Classical Cepheids (delta Cep class, DCEPs) in the dense central regions of the Large and Small Magellanic Clouds (LMC and SMC). We analysed J and Ks time-series data covering the central 1.77 deg^2 of each galaxy. Utilising approximately 40 epochs per filter and PSF-based photometry, we derived high-quality light curves for 573 and 2090 DCEPs in the LMC and SMC, respectively. We derived exceptionally precise PL and PW relations, exhibiting the lowest photometric dispersion published so far for the Magellanic Clouds. Fourier parameters calculated from the light curves indicate that pulsational models incorporating a mildly non-canonical mass-luminosity relation and a mixing-length parameter of alpha = 1.7 best reproduce the observations. Age derivations confirm a bimodal star formation history in the SMC centre. Crucially, we discovered a striking line-of-sight spatial dichotomy within the young SMC DCEP population (t < 116 Myr), which is bifurcated into two distinct structures separated by ~4 kpc. This provides independent stellar evidence tracing a recent direct collision with the LMC. Finally, by unifying fundamental and first-overtone pulsators, we derived a highly constrained relative distance between the Clouds. Comparing this to detached eclipsing binary distances, our data suggest a moderate metallicity correction for the Leavitt Law with gamma ~ -0.2 mag/dex.

title: Mitigating variance shrinkage in multi-task galaxy property inference from imaging data via statistical manifold alignment
comment: 12 pages, 5 figures, 2 tables, accepted by A&A
summary: Inferring photometric redshifts ($z$) and key stellar population properties ($\log(M_*/\mathrm{M}_\odot)$, $D_n4000$, and $\mathrm{H}δ_A$) directly from multi-band imaging is increasingly critical for spectroscopically limited large surveys such as LSST and CSST. However, conventional point-wise loss functions (e.g., mean squared error or Huber loss) employed in deep neural networks often induce ``variance shrinkage''---a regression-to-the-mean effect that contracts predicted variances, distorts non-linear physical manifolds (such as bimodal distributions), and truncates heavy-tail populations. Here, we present ViTMultiTask, a vision transformer framework that incorporates a multi-scale maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) loss to enforce higher-order joint distribution alignment in reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS). Trained on 83,846 galaxies from Subaru HSC five-band ($g,r,i,z,y$) imaging cross-matched with DESI Data Release 1 Bright Galaxy Survey spectra, the model achieves high point-estimate precision on an independent test set of 5,000 galaxies: $σ_{\mathrm{NMAD}} = 0.020$ for $z$, $0.169\,\mathrm{dex}$ for $\log(M_*/\mathrm{M}_\odot)$, $0.073$ for $D_n4000$, and $1.185\,\text{Å}$ for $\mathrm{H}δ_A$. Ablation experiments demonstrate that incorporating the MMD loss effectively mitigates variance shrinkage and more accurately reproduces the observed spectroscopic parameter distributions (including bimodal structures and heavy tails), while maintaining point-estimate accuracy statistically consistent with the baseline (RMSE changes $\le 3.5\%$) and catastrophic outlier rates fully comparable to the baseline. This kernel-based manifold alignment offers a statistically grounded and practical paradigm for comprehensive galaxy property inference in the deep imaging era.

title: A Multi-Cycle Treasury Survey of Andromeda: Comprehensive, All-Encompassing Spectroscopy, Imaging, and Mid-Infrared Mapping of the Nearest Giant Spiral
comment: A White Paper submission on Multi-Cycle Treasury Program Concepts with JWST, comments welcome
summary:
We propose a Multi-Cycle Treasury program of $\sim$800 hours that would survey Andromeda the way the Milky Way has been surveyed by APOGEE, Gaia, and WISE.
  - NIRSpec: spectra of $\sim$4,500 red giants and supergiants at S/N~80, sufficient for 16 elements at $\lesssim$0.05 dex precision and radial velocities to a few km s$^{-1}$.
  - NIRCam: $\sim$1,600 arcmin$^{2}$ in up to ten filters, reaching $\sim$20 million stars, every field imaged twice a year apart: two-epoch infrared photometry of the $\sim$500 Cepheids and $\sim$10$^{4}$ Miras in the footprint.
  - MIRI: $\sim$450 arcmin$^{2}$ in five filters at the depth of PHANGS.
  The observations are predominantly organized as twelve "bricks", each of three adjacent fields including two NIRSpec/MOS pointings, in which one instrument is prime and a second observes in parallel, so that roughly 40% of the exposure time comes at no charge. The bricks sample the nucleus, bulge, major axis to 29 kpc, minor axis, and inter-arm disk. In addition, a 100-hour grid of short NIRCam pointings with MIRI in parallel covers the HST-PHAT footprint. The result would be the first chemodynamical, star-formation, and dust map of an $L^{\star}$ galaxy other than our own built from individual stars, at a scale no single-cycle program can reach.

title: Dissecting and diagnosing the LISA Galactic binary population
comment: 17 pages, 15 figures
summary: LISA will individually resolve thousands of Galactic double white dwarf (DWD) binaries, while the majority stays buried in an unresolved gravitational wave (GW) confusion foreground. Which systems get resolved depends on the binary's parameters, on the global population and on instrumental sensitivity, so the resolved population is not a representative sample of the underlying Galactic population. Interpreting LISA's future catalog therefore requires understanding these selection effects. Here we characterize the resolved and unresolved subpopulations of a simulated Milky Way DWD catalog, using an iterative subtraction pipeline applied over different observation times. Resolvability is driven primarily by chirp mass: higher chirp mass, inspiraling systems are strongly favored over lower mass, outspiraling or monochromatic ones, and this reflects on the rate with which different composition subtypes are resolved. Spatially, resolved sources trace the Galactic bulge, because it is intrinsically the densest region of the Galaxy. The confusion background shows an internal bimodal chirp-mass structure, and is not generated uniformly by the same subpopulation in different frequency bands. We introduce a diagnostic for the minimum number of sources needed to reproduce a given fraction of the confusion power in a frequency band, and show that a residual confusion floor persists even after 100 years of integration. These biases are significant and need to be accounted for when using LISA's resolved DWD catalog and the confusion background to constrain the Galactic DWD population.

title: Swept by the Galactic Tide: How Galactic Tides and Stellar Encounters Drive the Evolution of Wide Binaries and Their Giant Planets
comment: 30 pages, 19 figures. To be submitted to AAS Journals. Comments welcome!
summary: Wide stellar binaries ($a_b > 10^3$ AU) are common throughout the Galaxy, and many host extrasolar planets. Comparing planets in wide binaries with those around single stars can reveal whether a distant stellar companion affects planet formation. Such a comparison cannot be made directly, however: unlike in single-star systems, the Galactic tide and passing field stars dramatically reshape wide binaries over Gyr timescales, influencing the orbital properties and stability of the planets they host. In this work, we present N-body simulations demonstrating how the Galactic tide and stellar encounters sculpt the orbits of super-Jupiters on 1-6.5 AU orbits in wide binary systems on Sun-like Galactic orbits over 9 Gyr. We predict systematically higher orbital eccentricities for planets in wide binaries compared to single-star systems, with the most significant differences in older systems and those with more massive binary companions. Planetary ejections and disruptions are also common, and we find that planet-hosting binaries with orbits nearly perpendicular to the Galactic midplane are preferentially depleted. In our most optimistic estimate, the maximum hot Jupiter production rate is enhanced by up to a factor of ~3 relative to binaries without Galactic perturbations. A significant fraction of these binaries are also ionized (the stars become unbound), with a preference for ionization in lower-mass binaries, while the eccentricity distribution of survivors relaxes from mildly superthermal to nearly thermal. These results provide testable predictions for the population of giant planets in wide binaries soon to be revealed by Gaia DR4 and DR5.

title: Satellite pairs in the Local Group: from spatial clustering to dynamical associations in observations and $Λ$CDM simulations
comment: Accepted for publication in ApJ on 17-10-2026. 30 pages, 12 figures, 8 tables
summary: We investigate the incidence and physical nature of satellite galaxy pairs in the Local Group using updated observational data for the Milky Way (MW) and Andromeda (M31), together with analogues from the HESTIA constrained cosmological simulations. Our comparison uses three distinct simulated Local Group analogues drawn from the HESTIA suite, allowing us to assess the observed pair statistics against multiple cosmological realisations of the Local Group environment. We identify close nearest-neighbour associations by comparing the observed satellite distributions with isotropic populations that reproduce the radial distributions of each host, and investigate their physical nature using line-of-sight velocities, proper motions, and gravitational binding estimates. We find that the MW exhibits a significant excess of close satellite associations relative to isotropic expectations, with a pairing efficiency of $\sim53\%$, nearly twice that found in the simulated analogues ($\sim17$-$27\%$). This excess persists after applying a stellar mass cut ($M_\star > 10^4\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$) to match the resolution limits of the simulations. In contrast, the M31 satellite system is broadly consistent with isotropy, with a pairing efficiency of $\sim28\%$. However, only a minority of pair candidates exhibit coherent kinematics or are likely to be gravitationally bound, indicating that most represent transient alignments or remnants of common group infall rather than long-lived binary satellites. These results suggest that the MW hosts an unusually rich population of phase-space-correlated satellites, likely reflecting its recent accretion history, whereas M31 is more consistent with typical $Λ$CDM expectations.

title: Magellan PFS Discovery of a Cold Gas Giant Exoplanet Likely Formed by a Gas Disk Gravitational Instability
comment: 17 pages, 5 figures, 1 table, in press, ApJ Letters
summary: Using the Planet Finder Spectrograph (PFS) on the 6.5-m Magellan Clay Telescope at the Las Campanas Observatory we have discovered a cold gas giant exoplanet orbiting the K7V dwarf star HIP88962. 16 yrs of PFS observations imply an exoplanet with an orbital period of $\approx$ 19.3 yrs and a radial velocity semiamplitude (K) of 94.9 m s$^{-1}$. With a host star mass of 0.62 $M_\odot$, this implies a planet mass $M_p sin(i) \sim 5 M_{Jup}$. While stable M dwarfs have a PFS RMS of $\approx$ 3 m s$^{-1}$, the single Keplerian fit for HIP88962 has an RMS of $\approx$ 6 m s$^{-1}$, hinting at a second exoplanet. The best double planet Keplerian fit, with a 4.113 d period, still results in a RMS of $\approx$ 5 m s$^{-1}$. HIP88962 has Ca II H lines with twice the emission of four stable stars, implying that stellar activity may contribute to the RMS jitter error for the single Keplerian fit. When combined with Hipparcos and Gaia astrometry, HIP88962 b has a nearly edge-on orbit with inclination 91 $\pm$ 22 deg, true planet mass $4.83$ M$_{Jup}$, semimajor axis 6.15 $\pm$ 0.5 au, and eccentricity 0.718 $\pm$ 0.02. Including a PFS jitter of $\approx$ 7 m s$^{-1}$ yields $χ^2 = 0.995$ for the combined solution. A massive gas giant orbiting at $\approx$ 6 au around a 0.62 $M_\odot$ star is incompatible with published core accretion population synthesis models, but consistent with formation by gas disk gravitational instability.

title: Active Learning for Molecular Discovery: A Retrospective Test toward TMC-1
comment: 13 pages, 3 figures, 3 tables; submitted to ApJ; code and data at doi:10.5281/zenodo.23312984
summary: Machine-learning recommendation lists can help prioritize searches for new interstellar molecules, but whether reranking such a list as detections accumulate improves on it has not been tested. We present a pre-registered retrospective test toward TMC-1, using a published machine-learning list of 1,510 recommended candidates, consolidated to 1,434 candidates, and the species reported there through September 2026. At four annual origins from 2022 to 2025, a logistic-regression ranking on seven released features, refit on the detections known at each origin, separates later detections from never-detected candidates with a pooled AUC of 0.867, against 0.706 for the best single-criterion baseline (difference 0.160; 95\% interval 0.095-0.230). The advantage persists under a shifted date boundary and two alternative feature regimes, but is not established among the top 100 candidates (12 versus 7 detections). A searcher that refits on its own observations reaches half of the 63 detected species on the list in a median of 200 observations, against 332 for the best fixed ordering and 717.5 expected for random search. Uncertainty sampling, the standard active-learning rule, performs worse than random (AUC 0.210): later detections lie at low predictive uncertainty, close to known chemistry. Of 101 species in our validation set, 37 are absent from the list, and only 13 of these appear in a pool rebuilt from its source databases, including 2 of 11 radicals and neither ion. Candidate generation, not ranking, is the main constraint. We release 100 recommended targets, with code and frozen inputs, for prospective testing.

title: Globular Clusters in the Time of JWST. II. Looks like the second, moves like the first: the syrphid-like intermediate population of NGC 2808
comment: 16 pages, 12 figures, submitted to MNRAS, comments welcome
summary: The present-day kinematics of multiple populations in globular clusters can retain information about their initial conditions and can therefore help trace how the different populations formed. We combine JWST and HST photometry and proper motions to study the internal dynamics of four populations in NGC 2808 out to about eight half-light radii: the first population (1P) and three second-population groups with increasing light-element processing (2Pa, 2Pb, and 2Pc), providing the first detailed kinematic characterisation of the chemically intermediate 2Pa. We find significant kinematic differences between the populations. While all four have similar sky-projected radial velocity dispersions, 2Pb and 2Pc have lower tangential dispersions than 1P and are strongly radially anisotropic, whereas 2Pa shares the only mildly anisotropic kinematics of 1P. Therefore, chemically distinct 2P groups have different dynamical properties, suggesting that they formed under different conditions and/or experienced a different subsequent dynamical evolution. In the outer JWST field, the velocity dispersion depends only weakly on stellar mass, with hints of inverted equipartition. The difference between radial and tangential equipartition is similar for 1P and 2Pa and decreases towards 2Pc, a trend that remains tentative given the uncertainties. Our results show that 2P is not a dynamically homogeneous group, and that the kinematics of its individual groups provide a key constraint for multiple population formation scenarios.

title: Magellanic Outflow and Chemistry Survey (MAGOS): the Outflow-Luminosity Scaling Relations in the Large and Small Magellanic Clouds
comment: 15 pages, 5 figures, 2 tables, accepted for publication in the ApJL
summary: Understanding massive star formation in low-metallicity environments is crucial for constraining the universality of star formation across cosmic evolution. In this Letter, we present the first systematic survey of massive protostellar outflows in the Large and Small Magellanic Clouds (LMC and SMC, $Z\sim$0.2--0.5 $Z_\odot$), as part of the Magellanic Outflow and Chemistry Survey (MAGOS). MAGOS targets 40 massive young stellar objects (MYSOs) with luminosities of (1--23)$\times 10^4$ $L_\odot$ with the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) at 0.85 mm at a linear resolution of $\sim$0.1 pc. Using CO (3--2), we identify blue- and red-shifted outflows associated with the primary continuum sources toward 29 targets in the LMC and 10 targets in the SMC. Comparing the outflow mass, momentum, energy, and force versus luminosity scaling relations in MAGOS with those in the Galaxy, we find that the LMC CO outflows have a similar slope in the mass-luminosity relation, suggesting that CO remains an effective tracer of massive protostellar outflows at $Z\sim$0.5 $Z_\odot$. In contrast, despite the large scatter, the SMC CO outflows are deficient at high luminosity and show flatter scaling relations than the LMC and the Galaxy. This is consistent with reduced CO abundances due to enhanced photodissociation at high luminosity and low metallicity ($Z\sim$0.2 $Z_\odot$), although the possibility of intrinsically weak outflow launching cannot be ruled out with the current data.

title: The origin of Potassium in Galactic chemical evolution - The effect of C-O shell mergers in massive stars
comment: 12 pages, 7 figures, submitted to Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary: The Galactic chemical evolution (GCE) of potassium (K) and of most other odd-Z elements remains poorly understood: models generally underproduce the observed [K/Fe] over a wide metallicity range, depending on the adopted massive star yields. A proposed site for efficient K nucleosynthesis is the merger between the oxygen and carbon shells (C-O shell merger) that can occur in massive stars a few hours before core collapse. Some GCE models with specific yield sets have been shown to reconcile predictions with observations. Here we re-analyse these yield sets to quantify the contribution of C-O shell mergers to K production and what the Galactic evolution of K implies about the occurrence of these events. We analyse 194 pre-supernova models from three independent yield sets, covering a wide range of initial masses, metallicities and rotational velocities, and including both single and binary-stripped stars. We identify the progenitors undergoing a C-O shell merger and compute GCE models with and without their contribution. In all three sets, the enhanced K production can be traced back to a small number of C-O merger progenitors, which eject up to ~10-50 times more K than non-merger progenitors of similar mass. Without them, no model reproduces the observations and [K/Fe] is sub-solar over most of the metallicity range. With them, [K/Fe] is enhanced only within the metallicity window where mergers occur in each grid. Binarity itself plays a minor role, as single stars alone produce similar amounts of K. Since the K synthesised in a C-O merger is essentially primary, the observed nearly linear increase of [K/H] with [Fe/H] can be reproduced only if C-O shell mergers occur with a similar frequency at all metallicities. K could therefore be used to infer the occurrence rate of C-O shell mergers in massive stars as a function of time.

title: Bidimensional Exploration of the warm-Temperature Ionised gaS (BETIS) III. The impact of eDIG on strong-line abundance determinations in galactic halos
comment: 16 pages, 8 figures, 1 table. Submitted to A&A
summary: The extraplanar diffuse ionised gas (eDIG) is a key tracer of the feedback processes that connect galactic discs and halos. We present the first study of spatially resolved gas-phase chemical abundances in the eDIG of edge-on galaxies, based on integral field spectroscopy obtained with MUSE. Using a sample of four galaxies from the BETIS sample, we derived maps of the oxygen abundance, 12+log(O/H), the nitrogen-to-oxygen ratio, log(N/O), and the ionisation parameter, log(U), with the HII-CHI-Mistry v5.5 code, and we tested the reliability of this method when different ionisation sources are present. We separated the eDIG into star-formation-dominated and shock-contaminated regimes according to the relative contribution of photoionisation and shocks, and investigated their impact on the derived chemical abundances. We find that HII-CHI-Mistry returns systematically lower O/H and N/O values in shock-contaminated regions, especially for N/O, with typical offsets of ~0.1-0.15 dex relative to star-formation-dominated regions, together with a more homogeneous and lower ionisation state (log(U) ~ -3.1). In contrast, star-formation-dominated regions span a wider range of ionisation parameters (log(U) ~ -3.3 to -2.8) while maintaining approximately solar oxygen abundances. Despite these differences, the abundance offsets are comparable to the sampling step of the HII-CHI-Mistry model grid. The inferred oxygen abundance shows little variation between discs and halos. This is compatible with a scenario in which star formation feedback and galactic fountains efficiently recycle oxygen-rich gas between both components, in agreement with hydrodynamical simulations. In contrast, the N/O ratio shows significant radial and vertical variations, particularly in environments with weaker star formation feedback.

title: Radiation, Thermochemistry, and Stellar Feedback in DISPATCH
comment: 19 pages, 11 figures, 3 tables
summary: The growth of massive stars depends on whether their accretion flows survive radiation and outflow feedback from the forming stellar population. We present an extension of DISPATCH that couples directional stellar radiation, diffuse infrared transport, and thermochemistry to self-gravitating magnetohydrodynamics, individual stellar accretion, and protostellar jets. This AMR-based method uses DISPATCH's local timestepping, allowing stellar environments and their larger scale cluster environments to step on separate timescales, and providing the framework needed to scale to long-duration simulations of GMCs. Direct radiation is transported in multiple bands, including both ionizing and nonionizing radiation, and uses short characteristics to maintain source directions and shadowing. Diffuse radiation is implemented for IR reprocessed light, with M1 and stationary ray options for transport. The thermochemical model includes atomic and molecular hydrogen and helium chemistry, and metal cooling and dust. It also includes a composition-dependent equation of state. Stellar masses grow through accretion of gas rather than a prescribed IMF, allowing stellar masses to respond to the evolving gas supply and feedback. In tests, multiple-source illumination retains geometric shadows while diffuse reprocessing heats shielded material, and tests of jets, ionization fronts, and radiation pressure demonstrate expected behavior and convergence. Ionization fronts also cross asynchronous refinement boundaries with late-time propagation speeds within a few percent of analytic predictions. Together, these developments provide a framework for determining how radiative and mechanical feedback modify the duration and efficiency of accretion from turbulent clouds, connecting the gas supply to individual stars with the high-mass stellar initial mass function.

title: Probing Ultralight Higher-spin Dark Matter using Stellar Kinematics of Dwarf Galaxies
comment: 10 pages, 10 figures
summary: Stellar kinematics of the classical Milky Way dwarf galaxies provide a powerful probe of the dark matter distribution and its underlying physics. In this article we use them to explore ultralight dark matter (ULDM) with a non-zero spin. Numerical simulations in the non-relativistic limit have shown that, for the same initial conditions, higher-spin ULDM forms a more diffuse soliton core at the galactic center, with a smoother transition to the NFW outer region, than scalar ULDM. We introduce a generalized parametrization of the ULDM halo profile that captures these spin-induced effects through three additional parameters: the normalization of the central core density, the exponent of the core-halo mass relation, and the radius of the transition to the NFW envelope. Applying this profile in a Bayesian analysis of six classical dwarf galaxies, we find halo masses in the range $10^{8.5}$-$10^{9.5}\,M_\odot$ and, from each galaxy individually, a particle mass $m \gtrsim 3\times10^{-21}$ eV. The core-halo exponent and the transition radius are consistent with their scalar values. The core-density normalization is also consistent with the scalar value in four galaxies and prefers a core denser than a scalar soliton in Fornax, while the factor-of-several suppression expected for higher-spin cores is not excluded by any single galaxy. The data therefore show no preference for the more diffuse cores of higher-spin ULDM, but do not yet rule them out.

title: The full Gaia colour-magnitude diagram with white dwarfs reveals a declining Milky Way star formation history
comment: Submitted to MNRAS, 20 pages main text + 4 pages appendix, 13 figures
summary: White dwarfs (WDs) provide a fossil record of the Milky Way star formation history (SFH) through the combined effects of stellar evolution and cooling. They have, however, generally been modelled in isolation from the non-degenerate population, so that no single self-consistent set of Galactic assumptions has been required to reproduce both. We present CALOMERA, a semi-analytic chemo-dynamical population synthesis framework in which the vertical density profiles of mono-age subpopulations are computed self-consistently with the Galactic potential and coupled to modern WD cooling sequences, metallicity-dependent progenitor lifetimes and synthetic photometry. We calibrate 18 parameters describing the initial mass function, SFH, initial-final mass relation and WD population against a Gaia DR3 sample of $7.98\times10^{6}$ stars within 1 kpc, including $1.1\times10^{5}$ WDs. The calibrated model reproduces the star counts in each colour-magnitude diagram region to within 3% and the total number count to within 0.5%, compared with the 81% excess in the predicted WD count obtained with the previous main-sequence-only calibration. The recovered SFH peaks early, declines exponentially thereafter, and includes two recent bursts, located at $τ\approx2.4$ and $0.5$ Gyr. Three cooling libraries (Montréal, BaSTI and LPCODE) yield comparably good fits, with differences confined to ${\rm M_G}\gtrsim15$ mag. The predicted luminosity function is in reasonable agreement with the 100 pc Gaia WD sample. We further predict the Galactic WD distribution and differential number counts for surveys of varying depth. Extending the framework to the substellar regime using ATMO models, we predict the Galactic L, T, and Y dwarf populations and their contribution to the deep JWST fields.

title: The ultraviolet continuum slopes of galaxies at $\mathbf{z \gtrsim 12}$ selected from ${\mathbf{0.6 \, deg}^2}$ of JWST imaging
comment: 16 pages, 8 figures, to be submitted to MNRAS
summary: We present an analysis of the ultraviolet (UV) continuum slopes $(β)$ of $55$ galaxies at $z\gtrsim 12$, selected from a wide-area ($>0.6$ sq. deg) search across publicly available JWST/NIRCam imaging. Our sample spans the absolute UV magnitude ($M_{\mathrm{UV}}$) range $-21.6 \leq M_{\mathrm{UV}} \leq -17.3$ and we find an inverse variance-weighted mean $\langleβ\rangle = -2.57\pm0.04$ indicating that, on average, the galaxy population is extremely blue at $z\gtrsim 12$. The average $β$ at these redshifts is consistent with the intrinsic stellar plus nebular continuum limit in the absence of UV dust-attenuation. Consistent with earlier JWST works, our analysis suggests that the moderately dust-attenuated galaxies at $z \lesssim 10$ become essentially attenuation-free by $z \simeq 11$. We find no evidence for a $β-M_{\mathrm{UV}}$ relation in our $z\gtrsim 12$ sample, indicating that the attenuation-free interpretation applies across all observed UV magnitudes. By augmenting our sample with previous JWST constraints down to $z=9$, and incorporating $M_{\mathrm{UV}}$-matched HST studies down to $z=4$, we find a smooth evolution in $β(z)$ over a wide range in redshift. The average value of $β$ becomes progressively bluer at $z>4$, with $\mathrm{d}β/\mathrm{d}z \simeq -0.1$. Finally, although we find that the typical galaxy at $z \gtrsim 12$ is consistent with the attenuation-free limit, the scatter in our individual $β$ measurements is consistent with the existence of a small population of dust-reddened galaxies with $β\gtrsim -2$.
